bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to taxation; sales and use; providing a temporary sales tax holiday in July 2026.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. [+SALES TAX HOLIDAY; TAX EXEMPTION ANNIVERSARY ACT. +]

[+(a) In honor of the 250th anniversary of the United States, the retail sale of tangible personal property is exempt from the tax imposed under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 297A, during the period from 12:01 a.m. on July 1, 2026, through 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026. +]

[+(b) For the purposes of this section, "tangible personal property" has the meaning given in Minnesota Statutes, section 297A.61, subdivision 10. Tangible personal property does not include alcohol, taxable cannabis products, or motor vehicles. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to taxation; sales and use; providing a temporary sales tax holiday in July 2026.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. SALES TAX HOLIDAY; TAX EXEMPTION ANNIVERSARY ACT.

(a) In honor of the 250th anniversary of the United States, the retail sale of tangible personal property is exempt from the tax imposed under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 297A, during the period from 12:01 a.m. on July 1, 2026, through 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026.

(b) For the purposes of this section, "tangible personal property" has the meaning given in Minnesota Statutes, section 297A.61, subdivision 10. Tangible personal property does not include alcohol, taxable cannabis products, or motor vehicles.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
additions: SALES TAX HOLIDAY; TAX EXEMPTION ANNIVERSARY ACT.

(a) In honor of the 250th anniversary of the United States, the retail sale of tangible personal property is exempt from the tax imposed under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 297A, during the period from 12:01 a.m. on July 1, 2026, through 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026.

(b) For the purposes of this section, "tangible personal property" has the meaning given in Minnesota Statutes, section 297A.61, subdivision 10. Tangible personal property does not include alcohol, taxable cannabis products, or motor vehicles.
This section is effective the day following final enactment.
